To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the palladium porphyrin complex can be synthesized from the palladium porphyrazine complex by the reaction with a suitable reductant, such as sodium amalgam, in the presence of a suitable acid.
the N(21), N(22)-bridged porphy-rin complexes of PdCl2 have a (μ-dichl-oro)dipallad-ium(II) structure and that the terminal PdCI2 moiety is approaching the porphyrins plane.
the N(21), N(22) bridged porphyrin complex of PdCl2 has the μ-dichloro structure, and that the Pd-Pd distance is shorter than that of the corresponding N(21), O(22) bridging.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of binuclear palladium(II) complexes of N(21), N(22)-bridged porphyins.
the synthesis, characterization, and properties of new palladium(II) complexes containing N(21), N(22)-bridged tetraarylporphyrins, and their use as catalysts for the oxidation of alcohols.
the development of novel porphyrin ligands with a view to the preparation of binuclear Pd(II) complexes, and the study of their catalytic activity for the oxidation of alkenes and arenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N(21), N(22) bridged porphyrin metallation with PdCl _{2} is an efficient way to prepare binuclear Pd(II) complexes with (μ-Cl) _{2} Pd _{2} structure.
the palladium complexes of N(21), N(22)-bridged porphyinogens are formed with a structure of (μ-dichlro)dipalladium in which the terminal moiety is coming to the porphryin plane.
the N(21), N(22)-ethenobridged porphyrins are not good bridging ligands for the formation of binuclear palladium(II) complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N(21), N(22)-bridged porphyin complexes are good precursors of the binuclear complexes.
the binuclear palladium(II) porphyrin complex is a useful catalyst for the oxidation of alkanes.
we have developed a new synthetic route for preparing binuclear palladium(II) complexes of porphyrins with a variety of N,N'-bridges.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the palladium complexes of N(21), N(22)-ethenobridged porphyrins are very stable and that they can be easily prepared by the reaction of the corresponding porphyrins with PdCl 2.
the N(21), N(22) ethylene bridge is a good bridge for binuclear palladium(II) complexation.
the N(21), N(22)-bridged binuclear Pd(II) complexes are more active catalysts for the Mizoroki–Heck reaction than the mononuclear ones.
